C-ESTABLISH-OPENWEARSYNC-BASELINE.IntentSummary: Publish the approved OpenWearSync architecture as versioned GRACE 4 durable context, a nine-module/five-data-flow graph and matching module verification contracts. This change is a documentation-and-contract baseline only: no Rust/Kotlin source, test implementations, build tooling or binary releases are written by this plan. After approval, separate scoped implementation changes can construct the final application without throwaway intermediate versions.

T-001.Title: Formalize product requirements and recording transfer invariants

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Write .grace/context/requirements.xml as normative one-way Samsung Voice Recorder transfer requirements with users, supported topology, lossless resume, no deletion, security and explicit acceptance outcomes.
Distinguish exactly-once durable file outcome from at-least-once delivery; define a stable-recording readiness rule and non-root app access verification gate.
Clearly separate user-confirmed facts from unverified client-isolation, MediaStore/SAF access, and overnight battery assumptions. Preserve unknowns as test gates rather than claims.

T-002.Title: Fix target technology and portable interface boundaries

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Update .grace/context/technology.xml to define shared Rust transfer/protocol/security core on Wear OS and Windows, Android NDK/JNI bridge, Kotlin Compose Wear UI, Android network/file/lifecycle adapter, Windows Rust Tokio/Axum receiver and Kotlin Compose Desktop UI.
Specify ownership and neutral protocol/FFI versioning, per-platform transport binding and keystore boundaries; do not invent a permanent native watch background daemon.
Define design-stage toolchain and future test categories while leaving exact unmeasured version/device support and cryptographic crate selections explicitly pending approval.

T-003.Title: Specify project engineering and battery/security principles

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Update .grace/context/principles.xml with contract-first GRACE governance, one target architecture without throwaway ports, Kotlin-owned Android scheduling, Rust as cancellable component and reviewed authentication.
Make idle, bounded discovery, no indefinite retry, release Wi-Fi requests and wake locks, protected original recordings and traceable failure paths explicit engineering principles.
Retain evidence-based safety and energy criteria: no claim that hotspot unicast, multicast, recording access, idle-drain target, or permissions have already been validated.

T-004.Title: Define release topology and Wear/Windows user-experience contracts

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Update .grace/context/deployment.xml with Wear OS APK/JNI and Windows Rust receiver/Compose Desktop packaging, local LAN and S25 Ultra hotspot topology, private firewall scope, pairing/revocation and install/update/release verification gates.

Update .grace/context/ux-guidelines.xml with circular Wear OS screens, one-action manual upload, progress/pause/cancel, pairing/connection/energy errors, accessible touch targets and Windows receiver status/history/settings.
Explicitly specify OS-cooperative opt-in automatic work and manual/saved endpoint fallback; address client isolation as a network blocker that a manually entered IP cannot bypass.

T-005.Title: Construct nine-module ownership graph and five explicit data flows

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Populate GD-MAIN in .grace/graph/main.xml with the nine M-* definitions in the approved spec and the five DF-* definitions: recording manifest, discovery/pairing, encrypted upload, durable checkpoints and lifecycle cleanup.

State for every module responsibility, dependencies, platform owner, exposed interfaces, invariants, linked modules, failure modes and cancellation or persistence behavior; avoid duplicating ownership across Kotlin and Rust.
Update .grace/graph/index.xml GD-MAIN Owns routing to include every and only those graph anchors; keep all semantic IDs as attribute-free XML tags.

T-006.Title: Create matching verification contracts and evidence gates

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Populate VD-MAIN with one V-M-* verification entry for each of the nine graph modules and route all entries via .grace/verification/index.xml.

Define observable deterministic integration/unit and security test contracts: non-privileged recording reads, Wi-Fi binding, hotspot client reachability, mDNS fallback, pairing, TLS identity pinning, chunk idempotence/resume/integrity, receiver crash/disk full, in-progress recording and exact-once durable file outcome.

Include real-hardware pending gates for overnight matched battery and temperature trials with thresholds, explicit setup and raw evidence requirements; do not label unexecuted gates passed. Each entry must have meaningful Scenario and TraceAssertion/Marker criteria compatible with GRACE 4.
Separate current documentary evidence from future executable product tests: don't reference fictitious build scripts or absent test files as already-running commands.

T-007.Title: Cross-check approved scope, ownership and open hardware uncertainties

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Cross-check GRACE requirements, graph, verification, architecture proposal and approved spec for one-to-one module/verification coverage, matching interface assumptions, ownership and requirements-to-gate traceability.

Do not convert unknown real-device facts into implementation guarantees; unresolved hotspot isolation, file access, network binding and thermal behavior must remain explicit release blockers or measurable test gates.
Reject changes outside the declared durable scope and reject any source code, project build manifests, undocumented new modules or unrequested features in this baseline change.

T-008.Title: Complete GRACE target-validation and prepare controlled application

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Run the external GRACE validation lifecycle against the selected baseline and target: pre-edit grace lint --path . --assertions baseline; after edits grace lint --path . --assertions target and grace lint --path . --parallel-preflight; run grace status --path . --json.

Verify actual lint diagnostics, projection ownership, cross-links, active bundle statuses, scope and selected target assertions without executing future app-level tests; record warnings and failures honestly.

Provide human review of all five context files, graph/verification indexes and routed documents. Do not mark this draft plan approved or mark the change applied without separate user approval and the GRACE execute/apply/archive lifecycle.
